scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window due to travel.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Linh Nguyen and I'm 64. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Ms. Nguyen, thank you for reaching out. I understand how frustrating it is to return from travel and find an unexpected charge. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with the account?
Sure, my account number is 8829-4401 and the email is linh.nguyen@email.com.
Thank you, Ms. Nguyen. I have pulled up your account. For security purposes, could you please confirm the last four digits of the payment method on file and your billing zip code?
The card ends in 4492 and my zip code is 90210.

Thank you for verifying those details. I see the cancellation was processed on the 34th day. Per our 'Service Terms and Refund Policy' (Section 4.2), refunds are typically restricted to requests made within 30 days of the charge. However, given your account history and the fact that this is your first such request, I can make a one-time exception to this policy.
Oh, that would be wonderful. Thank you so much for understanding my situation.

You are very welcome. I have processed the refund of $49.99 back to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit appear in your bank account within 3-5 business days depending on your financial institution. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?
No, that is everything. Thank you for your help!
It was my pleasure, Ms. Nguyen. Thank you for being a valued customer, and I hope you have a great rest of your day.

resolution_summary: Agent verified the customer's identity and account, acknowledged the policy violation, but exercised authority to grant a one-time exception for a refund.
